question: The Haripura session (1938) of the Congress, presided over by Subhas Chandra Bose, discussed the setting up of a National Planning Committee under the chairmanship of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At Haripura (Gujarat) in 1938, Subhas Chandra Bose's presidency saw the idea of a National Planning Committee taken up, and Jawaharlal Nehru was made its chairman (हरिपुरा अधिवेशन 1938 — राष्ट्रीय योजना समिति, अध्यक्ष जवाहरलाल नेहरू)

 

• The Committee was set up in October 1938 to prepare a blueprint for industrial development, with economists, scientists and industrialists as members.

 

• Bose, in his address, urged socialist planning and rejected the federal part of the Government of India Act, 1935.

 

• Haripura was a small village in Surat district, chosen to emphasise the Congress's rural connection.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bose was welcomed at Haripura with a procession of 51 bullock carts, a symbol of the rural flavour of the session.

 

• The Planning Committee's work was disrupted by the outbreak of the Second World War and Nehru's later imprisonment.

 

• K.T. Shah served as the Committee's secretary.

 

• The ideas of the Committee influenced the later Bombay Plan and the Planning Commission set up in 1950.

 

NOTE

 

• M. Visvesvaraya (Option 1): Visvesvaraya, the famous engineer, advocated planned economy through his book 'Planned Economy for India' but he was not the chairman of the Committee set up through the Congress.

 

• Vallabhbhai Patel (Option 2): Patel was known for organising the Congress and later integrating princely states. He did not head the planning body discussed at Haripura.

 

• Rajendra Prasad (Option 4): Rajendra Prasad took over from Bose in 1939 as Congress President and later chaired the Constituent Assembly. He did not head the National Planning Committee.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Tripuri session (1939) of the Congress.

1. Subhas Chandra Bose was re-elected President by defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya, the candidate supported by Gandhi.

2. After Bose resigned, Rajendra Prasad became the President.

3. After the session, Bose formed the Swaraj Party.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Bose won the 1939 presidential contest against Pattabhi Sitaramayya, whom Gandhi's group backed, and Gandhi remarked that Pattabhi's defeat was his own (त्रिपुरी अधिवेशन 1939 — सुभाष बोस की पुनर्निर्वाचन, पट्टाभि की हार)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: after differences with the Working Committee, Bose resigned and Rajendra Prasad was chosen President.

 

• Statement 3 is wrong: Bose founded the Forward Bloc in 1939, while the Swaraj Party had been formed in 1923 by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru.

 

• The Tripuri session, held near Jabalpur in the Central Provinces, was also marked by Bose's illness, as he attended it on a stretcher.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Forward Bloc aimed to unite all radical and anti-imperialist forces within India.

 

• The dispute at Tripuri arose over the Pant resolution, which asked Bose to form his Working Committee in accordance with Gandhi's wishes.

 

• Bose later formed the Indian National Army in South-East Asia in 1943.

 

• Tripuri is in Madhya Pradesh, a state formed in 1956.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): This set adds the false Swaraj Party claim and drops the correct account of Bose's re-election. The Swaraj Party is of 1923, so Bose could not have formed it after Tripuri.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): This combination accepts the Swaraj Party claim and drops the Pattabhi contest. Bose formed the Forward Bloc, so statement 3 is incorrect, and a set containing it fails.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Selecting all three overlooks that statement 3 is wrong. Bose's post-Tripuri organisation was the Forward Bloc, and the Swaraj Party dates back to the early 1920s.

question: Who served as President of the Indian National Congress continuously from 1940 to 1946, the longest unbroken term in the pre-independence period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abul Kalam Azad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Maulana Abul Kalam Azad presided over the Ramgarh session of 1940 and continued as President until 1946, the longest continuous tenure of the pre-independence era (अबुल कलाम आज़ाद — 1940 से 1946, सबसे लंबा कार्यकाल)

 

• His term was extended because no regular sessions were held in 1941-45, as the Congress was declared illegal after the Quit India Movement of 1942 and its leaders jailed.

 

• Azad was imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort with other leaders during that period.

 

• He led the Congress team at the Cabinet Mission talks of 1946 before handing over to Nehru in July 1946.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ramgarh is in present-day Jharkhand, then part of Bihar.

 

• The Muslim League passed the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution in March 1940, shortly before the Ramgarh session.

 

• Azad opposed the partition of India until the end.

 

• His book 'India Wins Freedom' was published in 1959.

 

• Maulana Azad was the youngest President in 1923 and the longest-serving of the pre-independence years, a rare double distinction among holders of the post.

 

NOTE

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 1): Nehru presided in 1929, 1936, 1937 and again in 1951-54, but in 1946 he took over only in July, so he did not hold a six-year unbroken spell before independence.

 

• Rajendra Prasad (Option 2): Rajendra Prasad was President in 1934, 1939 (after Bose) and later in 1947-48 after Kripalani resigned. His terms were each short, not a long unbroken period.

 

• Madan Mohan Malaviya (Option 4): Malaviya was chosen President for four separate sessions between 1909 and 1933, and none of these terms ran six years in a row.

question: The Meerut session of the Congress in 1946, the last session before Independence, was presided over by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is J.B. Kripalani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acharya J.B. Kripalani presided over the Meerut session of November 1946, the last Congress session before Independence (मेरठ अधिवेशन 1946 — अध्यक्ष जे.बी. कृपलानी)

 

• He was elected at a time when the Interim Government had taken shape under Nehru and negotiations on the transfer of power were underway.

 

• Kripalani was the Congress President when India became independent on 15 August 1947 and when Partition was accepted.

 

• He resigned in November 1947 after differences with the Government and Gandhi's suggestions over the party's role.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kripalani was an associate of Gandhi at Champaran in 1917.

 

• He later founded the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party in 1951 and then served in the Praja Socialist Party.

 

• His wife Sucheta Kripalani became Uttar Pradesh's Chief Minister in 1963, the first woman Chief Minister of an Indian state.

 

• After Kripalani, Rajendra Prasad took temporary charge, followed by Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Jaipur in 1948.

 

NOTE

 

• Pattabhi Sitaramayya (Option 1): Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the Jaipur session in 1948, after Independence. He was not the President at Meerut in 1946.

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru (Option 2): Nehru took over from Azad in July 1946 for a brief stint, but the Meerut session later that year was chaired by Kripalani, and Nehru was then the head of the Interim Government.

 

• Abul Kalam Azad (Option 3): Azad was President until July 1946 and had presided at Ramgarh 1940. He was no longer in the chair at the Meerut session in November 1946.

question: The first Congress session after Independence (Jaipur, 1948) was presided over by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the Jaipur session of 1948, the first regular Congress session after Independence (जयपुर अधिवेशन 1948 — अध्यक्ष पट्टाभि सीतारमैया)

 

• He was a doctor from Andhra, author of 'History of the Indian National Congress', and had been Gandhi's candidate against Bose in 1939.

 

• The Jaipur meeting took place after Gandhi's assassination in January 1948 and reviewed the party's role in a free India.

 

• The session also discussed linguistic reorganisation of states, which led to the JVP committee (Jawaharlal, Vallabhbhai, Pattabhi) in December 1948.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The JVP Committee advised postponing the formation of linguistic provinces.

 

• Pattabhi Sitaramayya founded the Andhra Bank in 1923 and later was Governor of Madhya Pradesh.

 

• Purushottam Das Tandon presided over the Nasik session of 1950 after defeating Kripalani.

 

• Dhar Commission (1948) had earlier reported against linguistic states.

 

• Pattabhi Sitaramayya had been jailed in 1942 at Ahmednagar Fort, where he wrote much of his history of the Congress, published in two volumes in 1935 and 1947.

 

NOTE

 

• Purushottam Das Tandon (Option 2): Tandon became President in 1950 at Nasik, two years after Jaipur, following a contest with Kripalani, who was Nehru's choice. He was not the Jaipur President.

 

• J.B. Kripalani (Option 3): Kripalani resigned in November 1947 after the Meerut period. By the time of Jaipur in 1948 the post had passed to Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

 

• Rajendra Prasad (Option 4): Rajendra Prasad held temporary charge after Kripalani's resignation in 1947, and then became President of the Constituent Assembly. He did not preside at Jaipur.

question: No annual session of the Indian National Congress was held between 1941 and 1945 mainly because:
option_1: The Congress had dissolved itself to join the Muslim League
option_2: The Cripps Mission had abolished the party organisation
option_3: War conditions and the banning of the Congress after the Quit India Movement left its leaders in jail
option_4: The Government of India Act, 1935 prohibited annual sessions
solution_text:
The correct answer is War conditions and the banning of the Congress after the Quit India Movement left its leaders in jail.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• No sessions took place in 1941-45 as the wartime situation and the ban on the Congress after the Quit India Movement (1942) put its leadership behind bars (1941-45 में कोई अधिवेशन नहीं — भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन के बाद कांग्रेस पर प्रतिबंध)

 

• The Quit India resolution was passed at Bombay on 8 August 1942, and the Government arrested the entire top leadership the next morning.

 

• Congress Working Committee members were kept at the Ahmednagar Fort and other jails until 1945.

 

• As a result Abul Kalam Azad, elected at Ramgarh in 1940, remained the President throughout, until 1946.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Congress was also faced with individual satyagraha in 1940-41 against India's involvement in the war.

 

• The Wavell Plan and the Simla Conference of 1945 followed the release of the leaders.

 

• Sessions resumed with Meerut in 1946.

 

• The Cripps Mission arrived in March 1942, before the Quit India movement.

 

NOTE

 

• The Congress had dissolved itself to join the Muslim League (Option 1): The Congress did not dissolve and never merged with the Muslim League; the two were rivals, and the League was demanding Pakistan in this period.

 

• The Cripps Mission had abolished the party organisation (Option 2): The Cripps Mission of 1942 offered post-war dominion status and failed to satisfy the Congress. It did not abolish the organisation, which launched the Quit India Movement afterwards.

 

• The Government of India Act, 1935 prohibited annual sessions (Option 4): The Government of India Act, 1935 dealt with provincial autonomy and federation. It said nothing preventing political parties from holding annual conventions.

question: How many delegates attended the first session of the Indian National Congress at Bombay in 1885?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 72.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The founding session at Bombay in December 1885 was attended by 72 delegates drawn from the Bombay, Madras and other presidencies (पहले अधिवेशन में प्रतिनिधि — 72)

 

• Most of the delegates were lawyers, journalists, teachers and landowners, giving the session the character of an educated, English-speaking gathering.

 

• The session met for three days from 28 December 1885 and passed nine resolutions, such as seeking an inquiry into the Indian administration and expansion of the legislative councils.

 

• The delegates' number rose steeply in later years, with 434 at Calcutta in 1886.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hume had planned the meeting for Poona, but plague there forced a shift to Bombay's Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College.

 

• W.C. Bonnerjee presided, and Hume was General Secretary.

 

• The resolutions of 1885 also demanded reduction of military expenditure and the holding of simultaneous civil service examinations in India.

 

• The Congress held every annual session in December in its first decades.

 

NOTE

 

• 134 (Option 2): 134 is not the figure recorded for the opening session; the attendance was just seventy-two. Numbers rose in later sessions, but this figure does not belong to the Bombay founding session.

 

• 434 (Option 3): This figure belongs to the second session at Calcutta in 1886, presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji. It is several times the attendance of the founding meeting a year earlier.

 

• 607 (Option 4): The Congress gathered a much larger body of delegates after the early years, and 607 is a figure that overstates the first meeting greatly, which had barely seventy-odd participants.

question: Who presided over the Gaya session of the Congress in 1922, after which the Swaraj Party was formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is C.R. Das.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chittaranjan Das presided over the Gaya session of December 1922, where he pressed for entry into the legislative councils (गया अधिवेशन 1922 — अध्यक्ष चितरंजन दास, स्वराज पार्टी)

 

• The No-Changers, led by C. Rajagopalachari, Vallabhbhai Patel and Rajendra Prasad, opposed council entry and defeated Das's proposal.

 

• Das and Motilal Nehru then formed the Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party in January 1923, after the Chauri Chaura withdrawal had caused disagreement.

 

• The dispute was settled at the Delhi special session of 1923 which allowed the Swarajists to contest elections.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• C.R. Das was called Deshbandhu and was a leading Calcutta barrister.

 

• He had been elected President in 1921 for the Ahmedabad session but was in jail.

 

• The Swarajists won many seats in the 1923 elections and in Bengal and the Central Provinces they had strong presences.

 

• Das died in 1925.

 

NOTE

 

• Motilal Nehru (Option 1): Motilal Nehru co-founded the Swaraj Party with Das, but he presided at Amritsar in 1919 and Calcutta in 1928, not at Gaya in 1922.

 

• Abul Kalam Azad (Option 2): Azad presided over the Delhi special session of 1923 that followed Gaya and reconciled the two groups. He did not chair the Gaya meeting.

 

• Hakim Ajmal Khan (Option 3): Ajmal Khan acted as President at Ahmedabad in 1921 as Das was jailed. He was not the President at Gaya the following year.

question: The Calcutta session of the Congress in 1928, presided over by Motilal Nehru, is associated with:
option_1: The declaration of Purna Swaraj as the Congress goal
option_2: The adoption of the Fundamental Rights resolution
option_3: An ultimatum to the Government to grant dominion status within one year on the basis of the Nehru Report
option_4: The endorsement of the Non-Cooperation Movement
solution_text:
The correct answer is An ultimatum to the Government to grant dominion status within one year on the basis of the Nehru Report.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Calcutta session of 1928 under Motilal Nehru accepted the Nehru Report and gave the Government a one-year deadline to grant dominion status (कलकत्ता अधिवेशन 1928 — नेहरू रिपोर्ट और डोमिनियन स्टेटस की समय-सीमा)

 

• Gandhi moved the compromise resolution, which was a softer position than the demand of Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Bose for complete independence.

 

• The deadline lapsed on 31 December 1929, and the Congress then turned to Purna Swaraj at Lahore.

 

• The Nehru Report had been drafted by a committee under Motilal Nehru, in answer to Lord Birkenhead's challenge to Indians to frame a constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Nehru Report of 1928 recommended dominion status, joint electorates and fundamental rights.

 

• Jinnah's Fourteen Points of 1929 were a reaction to the Report.

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Bose formed the Independence for India League in 1928.

 

• The Simon Commission had arrived in February 1928, causing protests.

 

• The Congress's one-year ultimatum of 1928 ended at midnight of 31 December 1929, and the Lahore session at once converted the demand into the goal of Purna Swaraj.

 

NOTE

 

• The declaration of Purna Swaraj as the Congress goal (Option 1): The Purna Swaraj declaration was passed at Lahore in 1929, a year after the Calcutta session, following the expiry of the dominion-status ultimatum. It was not the outcome of the Calcutta meeting.

 

• The adoption of the Fundamental Rights resolution (Option 2): The Fundamental Rights resolution was adopted at Karachi in 1931. Calcutta in 1928 took up the Nehru Report's constitutional proposals, which merely listed such rights in the draft.

 

• The endorsement of the Non-Cooperation Movement (Option 4): The Non-Cooperation Movement was endorsed at the special Calcutta session of 1920 under Lajpat Rai and confirmed at Nagpur. The 1928 session dealt with a constitutional proposal.

question: Which session of the Congress in 1920 amended the Congress constitution, defining its goal as the attainment of Swaraj by peaceful and legitimate means?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagpur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The regular Nagpur session of December 1920, presided over by C. Vijayaraghavachariar, changed the Congress creed to Swaraj by peaceful and legitimate means (नागपुर अधिवेशन 1920 — कांग्रेस का नया संविधान)

 

• The new constitution made the Congress a mass organisation, with a membership fee of four annas and a smaller Working Committee.

 

• Provincial Congress Committees were reorganised on a linguistic basis, a step that spread the party deep into the regions.

 

• The session confirmed the Non-Cooperation resolution passed at the Calcutta special session in September 1920.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Before 1920 the Congress goal had been stated as self-government within the Empire by constitutional means.

 

• C.R. Das moved the Non-Cooperation resolution at Nagpur, after he had opposed it in Calcutta.

 

• Nagpur's regular session came after the special session of 1920 at Calcutta.

 

• The Congress Working Committee set up at Nagpur had fifteen members.

 

NOTE

 

• Lucknow (Option 1): Lucknow in 1916 saw the reunion of Moderates and Extremists and the Pact with the League. It did not frame the 1920 creed, which was written four years later.

 

• Surat (Option 3): Surat in 1907 is remembered for the break between Moderates and Extremists. The creed framed at the Allahabad Convention of 1908 spoke of self-government within the Empire, not of Gandhian methods.

 

• Amritsar (Option 4): Amritsar in 1919 condemned the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and criticised the Reforms. The change of creed was effected a year later at Nagpur, not Amritsar.

question: Who acted as the President of the Ahmedabad session of the Congress in 1921, since the elected President C.R. Das was in jail?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hakim Ajmal Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hakim Ajmal Khan acted as the President of the Ahmedabad session of 1921 in place of the jailed C.R. Das (अहमदाबाद अधिवेशन 1921 — कार्यवाहक अध्यक्ष हकीम अजमल खां)

 

• The session was held when thousands of Congress workers, including leading leaders, were in prison for non-cooperation and Khilafat activities.

 

• Hasrat Mohani moved a resolution seeking complete independence at this session, which was not accepted, as Gandhi opposed it.

 

• Ajmal Khan was also the founder of Jamia Millia Islamia in 1920 and was a noted physician (Unani).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ajmal Khan was Chairman of the Reception Committee of the Delhi special session of 1923.

 

• He was the first Chancellor of Jamia Millia Islamia, after Gandhi laid the foundation.

 

• Hasrat Mohani coined the slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad' in 1921.

 

• Das's presidency in 1921 followed his imprisonment in December that year.

 

NOTE

 

• Mohammad Ali Jauhar (Option 1): Mohammad Ali Jauhar was jailed in this period and later presided at Kakinada in 1923. He did not act as President at Ahmedabad in 1921.

 

• Vallabhbhai Patel (Option 2): Patel was chairman of the Reception Committee at Ahmedabad, being Ahmedabad's municipal leader, but he was not the acting President.

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai (Option 3): Lajpat Rai presided over the Calcutta special session in 1920 and was himself jailed in December 1921. He was not the acting President at Ahmedabad.

question:
Match the Congress session with its President.

Column A: (a) Lucknow, 1916 (b) Amritsar, 1919 (c) Kanpur, 1925 (d) Karachi, 1931

Column B: (i) Sarojini Naidu (ii) Vallabhbhai Patel (iii) Motilal Nehru (iv) Ambika Charan Mazumdar
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lucknow session of 1916 was chaired by Ambika Charan Mazumdar, so a goes with iv (सत्र और अध्यक्ष का मिलान)

 

• At Amritsar in 1919, Motilal Nehru was President, matching b with iii.

 

• The Kanpur session of 1925 was presided over by Sarojini Naidu, the first Indian woman to head the Congress, so c is i.

 

• Vallabhbhai Patel presided over the Karachi session of 1931, giving d-ii.

 

• The four correct pairs are a-iv, b-iii, c-i and d-ii.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lucknow 1916 saw the Congress-League Pact, Amritsar 1919 condemned the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

 

• Kanpur 1925 was the venue where the Communist Party of India held its first conference in the same month.

 

• Karachi 1931 adopted the Fundamental Rights resolution.

 

• Patel became the first Deputy Prime Minister of India in 1947.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii (Option 2): This reverses the Lucknow and Amritsar Presidents. Mazumdar chaired the 1916 session and Motilal the 1919 one, so assigning them the other way round is wrong.

 

• a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i (Option 3): This pairs Kanpur with Patel and Karachi with Naidu. In fact Naidu presided over Kanpur in 1925 while Patel presided over Karachi in 1931, so the last two pairs are swapped.

 

• a-i, b-iii, c-iv, d-ii (Option 4): This mixes up three sessions. Lucknow was not presided over by Naidu, and Amritsar's President was Motilal Nehru rather than Mazumdar, so the scheme is wrong.

question:
Arrange the following Congress sessions in chronological order.

1. Karachi

2. Lucknow (Pact with Muslim League)

3. Lahore (Purna Swaraj)

4. Amritsar
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2, 4, 3, 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lucknow session with the Congress-League Pact came first, in 1916 (कालक्रम — लखनऊ 1916, अमृतसर 1919, लाहौर 1929, कराची 1931)

 

• The Amritsar session of December 1919 followed, after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

 

• The Lahore session of December 1929 declared Purna Swaraj as the goal.

 

• The Karachi session of March 1931 passed the Fundamental Rights resolution and was the last of the four.

 

• The correct order is Lucknow, Amritsar, Lahore, Karachi, which is 2, 4, 3, 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Between Amritsar and Lahore came Calcutta special (1920), Nagpur, Ahmedabad, Gaya, Delhi, Kakinada, Belgaum and Kanpur.

 

• Gandhi's Dandi March began between the Lahore and Karachi sessions, in March 1930.

 

• No session was held in 1930, owing to the Civil Disobedience Movement.

 

• The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931, shortly before the Karachi session.

 

NOTE

 

• 2, 4, 1, 3 (Option 1): This puts Karachi before Lahore. Karachi's session took place in 1931, two years after Lahore's declaration of Purna Swaraj, so the last two are reversed.

 

• 4, 2, 3, 1 (Option 2): This places Amritsar after Lahore. The Amritsar meeting was in 1919, ten years ahead of Lahore, making the middle part of the sequence incorrect.

 

• 2, 3, 4, 1 (Option 3): This begins correctly but puts Lahore before Amritsar and Karachi at the end. Amritsar, in 1919, preceded Lahore of 1929, so two items are misplaced.

question:
Arrange the following Congress sessions in chronological order.

1. Haripura

2. Ramgarh

3. Faizpur

4. Tripuri
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3, 1, 4, 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Faizpur (December 1937) came first, being the first session in a village (क्रम — फैजपुर 1937, हरिपुरा 1938, त्रिपुरी 1939, रामगढ़ 1940)

 

• Haripura followed in 1938 under Subhas Bose.

 

• Tripuri was held in March 1939, when Bose was re-elected and later resigned.

 

• Ramgarh in March 1940, with Azad presiding, was the last of the group.

 

• The order is thus 3, 1, 4, 2.

 

• Because the Lucknow Pact session fell in 1916 and the Amritsar session in 1919, those two take the first two places, and the 1929 and 1931 meetings follow in their natural order.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lucknow (1936) preceded Faizpur, with Nehru the President in both years.

 

• The Second World War started in September 1939, between Tripuri and Ramgarh.

 

• Bose's two sessions were in successive years, 1938 and 1939.

 

• Ramgarh was the last session before the five-year gap of 1941-45.

 

• Congress sessions between Amritsar and Lahore included Calcutta special, Nagpur, Ahmedabad, Gaya, Delhi, Kakinada, Belgaum, Kanpur, Guwahati, Madras and Calcutta again.

 

NOTE

 

• 3, 4, 1, 2 (Option 2): This reverses Haripura and Faizpur at the start. Faizpur, in December 1937, was held before the Haripura session of 1938, so the opening of the series is wrong.

 

• 1, 3, 4, 2 (Option 3): Here Tripuri is placed before Haripura. Bose presided over Haripura in 1938 and Tripuri in 1939, so that pair is the wrong way round.

 

• 3, 1, 2, 4 (Option 4): This puts Ramgarh before Tripuri. Tripuri took place in 1939, while Ramgarh was in 1940, so those two final items have been swapped.

question:
Assertion (A): The Surat session of the Congress (1907) was suspended without passing any resolution.

Reason (R): The Moderates and Extremists clashed over the choice of the President and the resolutions on Swadeshi and Boycott.

Choose the correct option.
option_1: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: A is false but R is true
option_4: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At Surat in December 1907 the Extremists and Moderates fought openly and the session was suspended without any resolution (सूरत अधिवेशन 1907 — बिना प्रस्ताव के स्थगित)

 

• Assertion A is true: the meeting ended in chaos, and no business could be transacted.

 

• Reason R is true: Extremists wanted Lajpat Rai as President and the 1906 Calcutta resolutions on Swadeshi and Boycott to be retained, while the Moderates, led by Pherozeshah Mehta and Gokhale, wished to drop them.

 

• The dispute directly caused the suspension, so R explains A.

 

• Tilak's demand to address the delegates was refused, and a shoe hurled on the platform brought the session to an end.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Moderates met in a Convention at Surat after the split, and framed the Congress constitution.

 

• Government repression increased after the split, and Tilak was jailed in 1908 in the Mandalay prison for six years.

 

• The Extremists were excluded from the Congress until 1916.

 

• The Allahabad Convention of April 1908 drew up the Congress creed.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 1): This claims R does not explain A, but the fight over the President's election and Swadeshi-Boycott resolutions was the immediate cause of the session's collapse.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 2): This says R is false. In fact the conflict over Rash Behari Ghosh's election and over the Calcutta resolutions on Swadeshi and Boycott was real, and it ended the session.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 3): This calls A false and R true. The session did end without any resolution, so the assertion is also true and the pair cannot be described this way.

question:
Assertion (A): The Karachi session of the Congress (1931) is remembered for its Resolution on Fundamental Rights.

Reason (R): It declared Purna Swaraj as the goal of the Congress for the first time.

Choose the correct option.
option_1: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true but R is false
option_4: A is false but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is true but R is false.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Karachi session of 1931 is indeed remembered for the resolution on Fundamental Rights and the economic programme, so A is true (कराची 1931 — मौलिक अधिकार प्रस्ताव; पूर्ण स्वराज लाहौर 1929 में)

 

• R is false, because the declaration of Purna Swaraj was made at the Lahore session of December 1929 under Jawaharlal Nehru.

 

• Karachi, under Vallabhbhai Patel, took place after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, and it also endorsed the Pact and Gandhi's participation in the Second Round Table Conference.

 

• As R is wrong, it cannot explain A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 1931 session also adopted a flag with the charkha and the three colours.

 

• Karachi is today in Pakistan's Sindh province.

 

• Patel's Karachi presidency followed his role in the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928.

 

• The Fundamental Rights resolution promised the abolition of untouchability and equality for all citizens.

 

• Purna Swaraj at Lahore (1929) and Fundamental Rights at Karachi (1931) are two separate milestones that are often confused, so they are best studied as a pair of consecutive landmarks.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A (Option 1): This calls R a correct explanation, but the Purna Swaraj declaration came at Lahore in 1929, so R is not even true of Karachi and cannot explain anything about it.

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 2): This accepts R as a true statement. The Purna Swaraj goal was declared at Lahore two years earlier, so R is false for Karachi in 1931.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 4): This option denies A though the Fundamental Rights resolution is the very reason Karachi 1931 is remembered, and it accepts R which belongs to Lahore.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Belgaum, 1924 – C.R. Das.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Belgaum session of 1924 was presided over by Mahatma Gandhi, not C.R. Das, so this pairing is wrong (बेलगाम 1924 — अध्यक्ष महात्मा गांधी, सी.आर. दास नहीं)

 

• C.R. Das presided over the Gaya session of 1922, where the council-entry controversy led to the formation of the Swaraj Party.

 

• The Calcutta session of 1917 under Annie Besant made her the first woman President.

 

• The Kanpur session of 1925 with Sarojini Naidu made her the first Indian woman President, and Motilal Nehru presided at Amritsar in 1919.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi presided at Belgaum, which was the only occasion he did so.

 

• Das was elected President in 1921 for Ahmedabad too but was in jail.

 

• Besant was released from internment in September 1917, just before the session.

 

• Both Naidu and Besant held office for one year each.

 

• Gandhi's presidency of 1924 was set apart from the others by its Hindu-Muslim unity fast of 21 days in September 1924 at Delhi, which preceded the Belgaum meeting.

 

NOTE

 

• Calcutta, 1917 – Annie Besant (Option 1): The pairing of Belgaum with C.R. Das is incorrect, and it is the answer to the NOT question; the Belgaum chair belonged to Gandhi, whereas Das presided over Gaya in 1922.

 

• Kanpur, 1925 – Sarojini Naidu (Option 3): The Calcutta 1917 pairing is right. Annie Besant, recently released from internment, was elected, making her the first woman President of the Congress.

 

• Amritsar, 1919 – Motilal Nehru (Option 4): Kanpur 1925 with Sarojini Naidu is a correct pairing, as she was the first Indian woman to preside, and is therefore not the odd one out.

question: Which of the following was NOT a European (non-Indian) President of the Indian National Congress?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Badruddin Tyabji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Badruddin Tyabji was an Indian, a Bombay barrister, and the first Muslim President (1887), so he was not a European President (यूरोपीय अध्यक्ष नहीं — बदरुद्दीन तैयबजी)

 

• George Yule (Allahabad, 1888) was the first British President.

 

• William Wedderburn presided twice, at Bombay in 1889 and Allahabad in 1910.

 

• Henry Cotton presided over the Bombay session of 1904, and Alfred Webb (Madras, 1894) was another non-Indian head.

 

• Tyabji's stand as the first Muslim President in 1887 makes him a notable Indian, which is why he is the only name here that does not belong to the list of European Presidents.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Wedderburn was an ICS officer who later served in the House of Commons and also chaired the Indian Parliamentary Committee.

 

• Cotton had served in Assam and opposed the partition of Bengal.

 

• Annie Besant (1917) and Nellie Sengupta (1933) were later non-Indian-born Presidents.

 

• Tyabji became a judge of the Bombay High Court in 1895.

 

NOTE

 

• George Yule (Option 1): Yule, a Scottish businessman, presided at Allahabad in 1888 and was a European, so he does not fit the question's exception.

 

• William Wedderburn (Option 2): Wedderburn was a Briton who held the post in 1889 and 1910. Being European, he is not the person the question asks for.

 

• Henry Cotton (Option 4): Cotton was a British former administrator who presided at Bombay in 1904. He was a European and so cannot be the odd one out.

question: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, founded in 1870, is associated with which of the following leaders?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahadev Govind Ranade.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870) was guided by Mahadev Govind Ranade, who was a judge and social reformer (पूना सार्वजनिक सभा 1870 — महादेव गोविंद रानाडे)

 

• It acted as a representative body of the people of the Deccan, sending petitions on land revenue and other grievances.

 

• Ganesh Vasudev Joshi, known as 'Sarvajanik Kaka', was another of its leaders.

 

• It was one of the regional bodies that preceded the Congress.

 

• Ranade also helped shape the early ideas of constitutional agitation, which later fed the Moderate programme of the Congress after 1885.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ranade was an active member of the Prarthana Samaj and founded the Indian National Social Conference in 1887.

 

• Tilak later worked with the Sabha, and then left it.

 

• The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha was among the first associations to use a systematic petition approach.

 

• The Sabha's journal was the Quarterly Journal.

 

NOTE

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji (Option 1): Naoroji led the East India Association in London and was associated with the Bombay Association. He had no part in building the Poona body of 1870.

 

• Jagannath Shankarseth (Option 2): Shankarseth founded the Bombay Association in 1852, almost two decades before the Poona body. He was not linked with the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha.

 

• Surendranath Banerjee (Option 3): Banerjee was the leader of the Calcutta-based Indian Association, which was founded in 1876. He belonged to Bengal, not to the Deccan-based Poona body.

question: The British Indian Association, one of the earlier political associations, was formed in 1851 in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcutta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The British Indian Association was formed in Calcutta in 1851, as a body of landholders and others in Bengal (ब्रिटिश इंडियन एसोसिएशन 1851 — कलकत्ता, बंगाल)

 

• It was formed through the merger of the Landholders' Society and the Bengal British India Society.

 

• Its newspaper, the Hindu Patriot, was edited by Harish Chandra Mukherjee.

 

• It petitioned for changes in the Charter Act of 1853, such as separate legislative councils.

 

• Founded just before the Charter Act of 1853 debate, the Association sent petitions to Parliament asking for a more representative legislature, which made it an important forerunner of the Congress.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Debendranath Tagore served as its secretary, and Radhakanta Deb as President.

 

• The Hindu Patriot became famous for supporting the indigo cultivators in 1860.

 

• The Association's membership was dominated by zamindars and wealthy professionals of Bengal.

 

• The Landholders' Society of 1837 was an even earlier political association, and it merged into this body.

 

NOTE

 

• Bombay (Option 1): Bombay's early body was the Bombay Association (1852) founded by Jagannath Shankarseth. The 1851 Association was set up elsewhere, in Bengal.

 

• Madras (Option 3): Madras had the Madras Native Association (1852) of Lakshminarasu Chetty. That is a different organisation from the British Indian Association.

 

• Poona (Option 4): Poona's body was the Sarvajanik Sabha of 1870 led by Ranade. It came nearly two decades after the 1851 Association and was based in Maharashtra.

question: Which of the following Congress Presidents presided over the Madras session of 1927, which resolved to boycott the Simon Commission?
solution_text:
The correct answer is M.A. Ansari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. M.A. Ansari presided over the Madras session of December 1927, which resolved to boycott the Simon Commission at every stage (मद्रास अधिवेशन 1927 — अध्यक्ष डॉ. एम.ए. अंसारी, साइमन कमीशन का बहिष्कार)

 

• The Commission, with no Indian member, was announced in November 1927 and arrived in India in February 1928.

 

• The Madras session also passed a resolution declaring complete independence to be the Congress goal, and asked for an All-Parties Conference to draft a Constitution.

 

• Ansari was a physician from Delhi, and a close associate of Gandhi in the Khilafat movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Simon Commission was headed by Sir John Simon.

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai was fatally injured in a lathi-charge during the protest at Lahore on 30 October 1928.

 

• Ansari was a founder of Jamia Millia Islamia in 1920.

 

• The All-Parties Conference led to the Nehru Report.

 

• Ansari later served as Chancellor of Jamia Millia Islamia, and he is chiefly remembered for the Madras session and his Khilafat work.

 

NOTE

 

• Motilal Nehru (Option 1): Motilal Nehru presided over the following session, at Calcutta in 1928, which took up the Nehru Report. He was not the President when Madras decided on the boycott.

 

• S. Srinivasa Iyengar (Option 2): Iyengar presided over the Guwahati session of 1926, immediately before Madras. He was the President of the year before the boycott decision.

 

• Annie Besant (Option 3): Besant presided in 1917 at Calcutta, ten years earlier. By 1927 she had left the Congress and was in her later years, so she did not chair the Madras session.

question: Who presided over the Calcutta session of the Congress in 1933?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nellie Sengupta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nellie Sengupta, the British-born wife of J.M. Sengupta, presided over the Calcutta session of 1933, held while the Congress was banned (कलकत्ता अधिवेशन 1933 — अध्यक्ष नेली सेनगुप्ता)

 

• The original President-elect, Madan Malaviya, was arrested on the way, and she took over the chair.

 

• She was the third woman, after Annie Besant and Sarojini Naidu, to preside over a session.

 

• The session met secretly, with police interference, as the Congress was banned under the Civil Disobedience Movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nellie Sengupta was born as Nellie Gray in Cambridge, England.

 

• Her husband J.M. Sengupta was a Bengal leader of the Congress.

 

• Sengupta stayed in India after her husband's death and contested elections.

 

• The Congress held the 1932 session in Delhi, also under police ban.

 

• Delhi in 1932 was presided over by Seth Ranchhoddas Amritlal, after Malaviya was arrested on his way to the session, and Calcutta in 1933 saw the same arrest and a similar replacement.

 

NOTE

 

• Annie Besant (Option 1): Besant had presided at the Calcutta session in 1917 as the first woman President, sixteen years earlier. The 1933 session had a different woman at the helm.

 

• Sarojini Naidu (Option 2): Naidu presided at Kanpur in 1925 and was not the person to preside at the Calcutta session of 1933, though she remained a prominent leader.

 

• Kamala Nehru (Option 4): Kamala Nehru, wife of Jawaharlal, was a freedom fighter and active in the Civil Disobedience Movement, but she never held the Presidency of the Congress.

question: Which of the following sessions of the Congress is correctly paired with a notable feature of that session?
option_2: Surat, 1907 – split between Moderates and Extremists
option_4: <style> @font-face { font-family: 'Hari'; src: url('https://static-appxdb-v2.akamai.net.in/fonts/HARI.TTF') format('truetype');} </style>Haripura, 1938 – first singing of Jana Gana Mana
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surat, 1907 – split between Moderates and Extremists.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Surat session of 1907 saw the Congress split into Moderates and Extremists, which is a correct pairing (सूरत 1907 — नरमपंथी-गरमपंथी विभाजन)

 

• Nagpur 1920 is famous for the new Congress constitution and creed of peaceful Swaraj, not for Purna Swaraj, which came at Lahore in 1929.

 

• Lahore 1929 declared Purna Swaraj, while the Fundamental Rights resolution is a feature of Karachi 1931.

 

• Jana Gana Mana was first sung at the Calcutta session of 1911, whereas Haripura 1938 is known for the National Planning Committee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rash Behari Ghosh presided at Surat.

 

• Nagpur 1920 was presided over by C. Vijayaraghavachariar.

 

• The Lahore session was held on the Ravi's banks.

 

• Haripura's President was Subhas Chandra Bose.

 

• Other sessions are also remembered for one defining feature each: Calcutta 1911 for the national anthem, Calcutta 1906 for Swaraj, and Calcutta 1917 for the first woman President.

 

NOTE

 

• Nagpur, 1920 – declaration of Purna Swaraj (Option 1): Nagpur in 1920 changed the Congress creed and constitution under Vijayaraghavachariar. The Purna Swaraj resolution is linked with Lahore in 1929, nine years afterwards.

 

• Lahore, 1929 – resolution on Fundamental Rights (Option 3): Lahore in 1929 declared complete independence as the goal. The Fundamental Rights resolution is the feature of the Karachi session of 1931, so this pairing is wrong.

 

• Haripura, 1938 – first singing of Jana Gana Mana (Option 4): Haripura of 1938 is known for the discussion on the National Planning Committee. The national anthem was first sung at the 1911 Calcutta session, so this pairing is wrong.

question: The Indian Association of Calcutta, founded in 1876, was established by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surendranath Banerjee and Anandamohan Bose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Association was founded in 1876 by Surendranath Banerjee and Anandamohan Bose, giving a more broad-based voice to the Bengal middle class (इंडियन एसोसिएशन 1876 — सुरेंद्रनाथ बनर्जी और आनंदमोहन बोस)

 

• It campaigned against the lowering of the age limit for the Indian Civil Service examination to nineteen in 1876.

 

• It organised the Indian National Conference in Calcutta in 1883, which was a forerunner of the Congress.

 

• The Association also took up the cause of peasants and later supported the Ilbert Bill.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Surendranath Banerjee toured India in 1877-78 to rally support against the ICS age limit.

 

• Banerjee presided over the Congress at Poona (1895) and Ahmedabad (1902).

 

• Anandamohan Bose presided over the Madras Congress session of 1898.

 

• Banerjee's journal was The Bengalee.

 

• Banerjee's 1877-78 tour of Indian cities built an all-India agitation, which created national sentiment before the Indian National Congress was formed.

 

NOTE

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji and Pherozeshah Mehta (Option 1): Naoroji and Mehta worked in Bombay, with Naoroji leading the London East India Association of 1866. They were not the founders of the Calcutta body of 1876.

 

• M.G. Ranade and G.V. Joshi (Option 2): Ranade and Joshi were prominent in the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha of 1870. They belonged to Maharashtra, not to the Calcutta-based Association.

 

• A.O. Hume and William Wedderburn (Option 3): Hume and Wedderburn were British associates of the Congress who helped found the Congress in 1885. They were not the founders of the Bengal body of 1876.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Presidents of the Indian National Congress.

1. Dadabhai Naoroji presided over four sessions.

2. William Wedderburn presided over the Congress in 1889 and 1910.

3. W.C. Bonnerjee presided at the first session in 1885 and again in 1892.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 and 3 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is wrong: Naoroji presided only three times, in 1886 at Calcutta, 1893 at Lahore and 1906 at Calcutta (अध्यक्षों के कथन — नौरोजी तीन बार, वेडरबर्न 1889 व 1910, बनर्जी 1885 व 1892)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Sir William Wedderburn presided at Bombay in 1889 and Allahabad in 1910.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: W.C. Bonnerjee was the first President in 1885 at Bombay and also presided at Allahabad in 1892.

 

• Hence only statements 2 and 3 hold true.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Wedderburn founded the Indian Parliamentary Committee in 1893 and was a Liberal MP.

 

• Wedderburn wrote the biography of A.O. Hume in 1913.

 

• Allahabad in 1892 came as the Indian Councils Act, 1892 was passed.

 

• Pherozeshah Mehta presided over the Calcutta session of 1890, a year after Wedderburn.

 

• Other early two-term Presidents of the Congress were Dadabhai Naoroji with three, W.C. Bonnerjee with two and Wedderburn with two, which are often tested together.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 2 only (Option 1): This accepts the false Naoroji claim of four sessions and denies Bonnerjee's two terms. Naoroji presided thrice, and Bonnerjee's second session was Allahabad in 1892.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): This pair includes the incorrect statement about Naoroji and omits statement 3. Bonnerjee did preside in 1885 and 1892, so leaving him out is a mistake.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): This accepts all three, though Naoroji presided three times, not four. Statement 1 is false, so this combination cannot be correct.
